la:verb:memini.gloss: to remember, recollect, recall, call to mind, think of
senses: to remember, recollect, recall, call to mind, think of
to be mindful of; to bear in mind
la:verb:memini.html:
mĕmĭni, isse, v. n.
Sanscr. man, think; upaman = Gr. ὑπομένειν, await; Gr. μεν- in μένω, Μέντωρ; μαν- in μαίνομαι, μάντις; μνᾶ- in μιμνήσκω, etc.; cf.: maneo, moneo, reminiscor, mens, Minerva, etc.
,
to remember, recollect, to think of, be mindful of a thing; not to have forgotten a person or thing, to bear in mind (syn.: reminiscor, recordor); constr. with gen., with acc. of the person and of the thing, with de, with a rel.-clause, with ut, with cum; with the acc. and inf. (usually the inf. pres., sometimes the inf. perf.; class.).
With gen.: vivorum memini,: constantiae tuae,: leti paterni,to be mindful of, not forget to revenge,.—
With acc.: suam quisque homo rem meminit,: praecepta facito ut memineris,: officium suum,: omnia meminit,: Cinnam memini,: numeros,.—With ellips. of acc.: neque adeo edepol flocci facio, quando egomet memini mihi (sc. nomen),.—
With de: de pallā memento,: de Herode,; .—
With a rel.-clause: meministi, quanta hominum esset admiratio,.—
With ut: meministin', olim ut fuerit vestra oratio?; .—
With cum: memini, cum mihi desipere videbare,.—
With acc. and inf.
With pres. inf. (so usually of the direct memory of an eyewitness): memini me fiere pavum, Enn. ap. Don. ad (Ann. v. 15 Vahl.): memini Catonem mecum disserere,: memini Pamphylum mihi narrare,: memini te mihi Phameae cenam narrare,; : meministis fieri senatusconsultum referente me,: mementote hos esse pertimescendos,: memento mihi suppetias ferre,.—So impers. memento with inf., remember to, i. e. be sure to, do not fail to: memento ergo dimidium mihi istinc de praeda dare,: ei et hoc memento (sc. dicere),: dextram cohibere memento,.—
With inf. perf. (so usu. when the subject is not an eye-witness; esp. with second and third persons of memini): peto, ut memineris. te omnia mihi cumulate recepisse,: meministis me ita distribuisse initio causam,: memineram ... divinum virum ... senile corpus paludibus occultasse demersum,: memini gloriari solitum esse Q. Hortensium, quod, etc.,: memento me,

son de meā, sed de oratoris facultate dixisse, .—Poet., of inanim. things: meminit lēvor praestare salutem,, .—

Absol., memini et scio, : recte meministi,your recollection is accurate,.—
Transf., to make mention of, to mention a thing, either in speaking or writing (rare but class.): meministi ipse de exsulibus,: neque omnino hujus rei meminit us quam poëta ipse,: Achillam, cujus supra meminimus. : sed tu, qui hujus judicii meministi, cur oblitus es illius,; : meminerunt hujus conjurationis Janusius Geminus in historia. M. Bibulus in edictis. ; .—Hence. mĕmĭnens, entis, P. a., mindful (ante- and post-class.): meminens corde volutat, Liv Andr ap P.: aevi, quod periit. meminens,: meminens naturae et professionis oblitus,.

la:noun:memoria.html:
mĕmŏrĭa, ae, f.
memor
.
The faculty of remembering, memory, recollection (class.): ubi me fugiet memoria,: Edepol, memoria's optumad,: bona,: segnis ac lenta,: tenacissima,: Hortensius memoriā tantā fuit, ut, etc.,: hoc in memoria mea penitus insedit,: in memoriam redigere,to recall to mind, recollect,; so, in memoriam reducere, memoriā comprehendere, to hold in the memory, commit to memory, id. do Or. 1, 34, 154: memoriā tenere,; : memoriā custodire,: memoriam agitare,to exercise the memory,: habere in memoriā,to remember,: hoc est mihi in memoriā,in my recollection,: deponere aliquid ex memoriā,to forget a thing,: memoriam alicujus deponere,to forget,: si memoria fefellerit,: hoc fugit memoriam meam,has escaped my recollection,: Carthaginem excidisse de memoriā,; cf.: memoriā cedere,: memoriā abire, ut mea memoria est, : ex memoriā exponam,from memory,.—
Memory, remembrance: si quid faciendumst mulieri male ... Ibi ei inmortalis memoriast meminisse,: verterunt sese memoriae, remembrances are altered, i. e. times are changed, : memoriā dign' viri,: nostrae,: memoriae prodere sermonem alicujus,to hand down to posterity, to leave in writing, to record,: memoriam prodere,to transmit, hand down,: traditur memoriae, prolapsum cecidisse,it is related,: vivit, vivetque per omnium saeculorum memoriam,: (oratio) ad memoriam laudum domesticarum,: quorum memoria et recordatio jucunda sane fuit,: memoria immortalis,.—
Transf.
The time of remembrance, period of recollection, time: multi superiori memoriā se in alias civitates contulerunt,in earlier times,: Cratippus princeps hujus memoriae philosophorum,in our time, at the present time,: quod persaepe et nostrā, et patrum memoriā acci dit,: usque ad nostram memoriam,: quod in omni memoriā est omnino inauditum,: post hominum memoriam,since the memory of man,: paulo supra hanc memoriam,a little before this, a short time since,.—
An historical account, relation, narration: liber, quo iste omnium rerum memoriam breviter complexus est,: de Magonis interitu duplex memoria prodita est,: memoriam vitae prosā oratione composuit,—
Concr., a written account, narrative, memoir: quispiam ex his, qui se ad litteras memoriasque veteres dediderat,: in veteribus memoriis scriptum legimus,; : sine ullā pristini auctoris memoriā,.—
(Eccl. Lat.) A monument, esp. a Christian church as a memorial of a saint or monument of a martyr: in memoriā Cypriani manere,: memoriae martyrum templis deorum succedunt, id. Civ. Dei, 26, 5; 22, 8, 11 and 12 al.: memoriam sibi et suis com parare,.—
Personified, the goddess of memory, = Mnemosyne, Afran. ap. : Jovis (filias, ex memoria uxore,, c. 37.

la:adj:memor.html:
mĕmor, ŏris (anciently memoris, memore, acc. to P.;
comp. memorior, P.), adj.
Sanscr. root smar-, in smarti, memory; smara, love; Gr. μάρτυς, witness; μέριμνα, care; cf.: memoria, mora, etc., not from memini
, mindful of a thing, remembering; constr. with gen., with acc. and inf., with a rel,clause, and absol.
In gen.
With gen.: ut memor esses sui,: se eorum facti memorem fore,: generis,: pristinarum virtutum,: quique sui memores alios fecere merendo,: nostri,; : vale nostri memor,.—
With acc. and inf.: memor Lucullum periisse,: memor objectum ab eo sibi,.—
With a rel. -clause: memor, quo ordine quisque discubuerat,: vive memor, quam sis aevi brevis,.—
Absol.: memorem et gratum esse,: et bene apud memores veteris stat gratia facti, grateful. : cf. 6, 664 supra: ipsa memor praecepta canam,; : pectus,.—Prov.: mendacem memorem esse oportet,a liar should have a good memory,.—
Trop., of inanim. things et cadum Marsi memorem duelli, which remembers the Marsian war, i. e. was made during that war, : medium erat in Anco ingenium, et Numae et Romuli memor,: lingua,: pectus,: auris,: cura,: manus,: saevae Junonis ira,vindictive, avenging,: supplicium exempli parum memoris legum humanarum,unmindful of, not observing,.—
Esp.
That easily remembers, possessed of a good memory: homo ingeniosus ac memor,.—
Poet., transf., that reminds one of a thing: nostri memorem sepulcro Scalpe querelam,: impressit memorem dente labris notam,: indicii memor poena,: tabellae,: versus,.—Hence, adv., in two forms.
mĕmŏre, by heart, readily (ante-class.): cum ista memore meministi, Pompon. ap. (Com. Rel. v. 109 Rib.).—
mĕmŏrĭter.
From memory, by personal recollection: oratio est habita memoriter,: omnes ordines memoriter salutavit,: Q. Mucius multa narrare de Laelio memoriter et jucunde solebat,.—
Esp.
With a good memory, by ready recollection: ista exposuisti, ut tam multa, memoriter, ut tam obscura, dilucide,: ut memoriter me Sauream vocabat,: hic quidem quae illic sunt res gestae memorat memoriter,: hem istuc si potes memoriter meminisse,; cf. Afran. ap. P. (Com. Fragm. v. 365 Rib.).—
Fully, accurately, correctly, ; : memoriter respondeto ad ea quae rogāro,: nostra Aratea memoriter a te pronuntiata sunt,; Auct. ad : tu, qui tam memoriter tenes omnes, (cf. Madv. ad ).

la:verb:memoro.html:
mĕmŏro, āvi, ātum (archaic
inf. pass. memorarier, ), 1, v. a.
memor
, to bring to remembrance, remind of, to mention, recount, relate, speak about or of, say, tell (class.).
With acc.: memorare mores mulierum,: nomen memora tuom mihi,: deos absentis testis memoras,callest on,: superbiam,: causas alicui,: antequam arma inciperent, misere legatos amicitiam obsequiumque memoraturos,; : patriam rhombi,.—Pass.: quid illa pote pejus muliere memorarier,: ubi ea, quae dico, gesta esse memorantur,: cujus conditor Hercules memorabatur,was said to have been, was remembered as,: memorari exempla,.—
With de: de naturā nimis obscure memoravit,.—
With acc. and inf.: quem infestum ac odiosum sibi esse, memorabat,: Herculem in eo loco boves abegisse memorant,: Mithridates, quem imperitasse Armeniis memoravi,: Palamedem memorant sedecim litterarum formas repperisse,.—
With a rel.-clause: musa, velim memores, quo patre natus uterque Contulerit lites,. —(ε) With sic: sic memorat,.—
Esp., to speak, utter, make use of in speech: scio ego multos memoravisse milites mendacium,: vocabula memorata Catonibus,.—
Memorare significat nunc dicere, nunc memoriae mandare, Paul. ex Müll.—Hence,
mĕmŏrātus, a, um, P. a., memorable, renowned, celebrated (poet. and in post-class. prose): ubi nunc nobis deus ille magister nequiquam memoratus Eryx?: locus Italiae ... fama multis memoratus in oris,; ; : sepulcrum memoratissimum,.—
Esp., before mentioned: dux,—
mĕmŏrandus, a, um, P. a., worthy of remembrance, memorable, celebrated (poet. and post-class.): juvenis memorande,.—Of inanim. and abstr. things: pugnae memorandae meae,: locus,: res,: exitus,.

senses: Lucius Marcius Memor, a Roman haruspex

la:noun:membrum.html:
membrum, i, n.
etym. dub.; perh. for mems-trum; cf. Sanscr. māmsa, flesh
,
a limb, member of the body (class.).
Lit.: jam membrorum, id est partium corporis, alia videntur propter eorum usum a natura esse donata, ut manus, crura, pedes, etc. . . . alia quasi ad quendam ornatum, ut cauda pavoni, plumae versicolores columbis, viris mammae atque barba,; : defessa,; : hispida membra,: membrum lacerum laesumve,: propter membrum ruptum talio,.—
In partic., = membrum virile, . So plur. membra, ; cf. ; , p. 254; .—
Transf.
In gen.
Of inanim. and abstr. things, a part, portion, division: omnes philosophiae partes atque omnia membra,: solvere quassatae parcite membra ratis,: per omnia philosophiae membra prudenter disputando currere,: eadem sunt membra in utrāque disputatione, —
Of persons: Ponticus . . . Bassus . . . dulcia convictūs membra fuere mei,: membra et partes alienae potentiae,; cf. poet.: fluctuantia membra Libyae,.—
Esp.
A member of the state: per multa membra civitas in unum tantum corpus redigitur,: membra partesque imperii,: reipublicae totius membra,: urbis,: Achaei scilicet per civitates velut per membra divisi sunt, unum tamen corpus et unum imperium habent,: corpore sic toto ac membris Roma usa. : cur ut decisa atque avulsa a corpore membra despiciar,.—
An apartment, chamber in a house: dormitorium membrum,a bed-chamber,: domūs membra,; , p. 188: modus membrorum numerusque,: cubicula et ejusmodi membra,.—
Of speech, a member or clause of a sentence: quae Graeci κόμματα et κῶλα nominant, nos recte incisa et membra dicimus, ; cf. .—
Of the Church of Christ: singuli autem alter alterius membra,; cf. the context: membra sumus corporis ejus,i. e. Christ's,.

la:adj:memorabilis.html:
mĕmŏrābĭlis, e, adj.
memoro
,
memorable, remarkable, worthy of being remembered; heard of, conceivable; worthy to be mentioned, fit to be spoken of (class.): vir,.—Comp.: memorabilior,: auctores,: nomen,: familiaritas,: virtus,: hoccine credibile est. aut memorabile?: nec bellum est, nec memorabile,: hoc memorabilest, ego tu sum, tu es ego,: in qua pugna illud memorabile fuit,: magni gutturis exemplum,.—Subst.: mĕmŏ-rābĭle, is, n., a noteworthy fact, strange occurrence (rare): multa memorabilia et in domesticis et in bellicis rebus effecerat,: hactenus de mundo ... nunc reliqua caeli memorabilia,.—Hence, mĕmŏrābĭlĭter, adv., memorably, remarkably, Aug. c. Jul. 2, 7, 11.

membrātim, adv.
membrum
,
by limbs or members, in the limbs, limb by limb, from member to member.
Lit.: membratim vitalem deperdere sensum,: nunc peractis malis, quae membratim sentiuntur, dicemus de his, quae totis corporibus grassantur,in single limbs,: caedere,in pieces,.—
Transf., piecemeal, singly, severally.
In gen.: membratim enumerare,; cf.: animalium naturae generatim membratimque ita se habent, § 1: gestum negotium,.—
In partic., of speech, in little clauses, in short sentences: dicere,; ; cf.: membratim caesimque dicere,: narrare,.

la:other:Memmius.html:
Memmius, a,
name of a Roman gens. mox Italus Mnestheus, genus, a quo nomine Memmi, . So C. Memmius, a public man, who, being adjudged guilty of ambitus, went into exile to Athens, to him Cicero addressed several letters, and to him Lucretius dedicated his poem, De Rerum Natura; cf. .—Hence,
Memmĭădes, ae, m., one of the Memmian gens, a Memmiade, a Memmius, .—
Memmĭānus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to a Memmius: praedia, of C. Memmius, .

la:noun:membrana.html:
membrāna, ae, f.
membrum
,
the skin or membrane that covers parts of the body (class.).
Lit.: natura oculos membranis tenuissimis vestivit,: cerebri,the membrane of the brain, meninges,: membranis cicadae volant,: membranis volant fragilibus insecta,.—
Esp., the skin or slough of snakes, ; .—
Transf.
The thin skin of plants and other things, : corio et membrana Punica (teguntur),: tenuissimis membranis velatur allium,: putaminis ovi,.—
A skin prepared for writing, etc., parchment, : Homeri carmen in Membrana scriptum,: sic raro scribis, ut toto non quater anno Membranam poscas, : Parrhasiae, for drawing,: croceae membrana tabellae,: quod in chartulis sive membranis meis aliquis scripserit, meum est,.—
The surface, outside of a thing (poet.): coloris,.—Trop.: scies, sub ista tenui membrana dignitatis quantum mali jaceat,.
